The appellants have filed the present Regular .

First Appeal, under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act'),
against the award dated 9.6.2016, passed by the Court of learned of Additional District Judge-II,
Shimla, Camp at Rohru (H.P.) (hereinafter referred to as 'the Trial Court'), in rt Land Reference Petition No. RBT-69-R/4 of 2014/08, titled as, 'Gokla Nand and others versus HPSEB and others'.

By virtue of award dated, 9.6.2016, the learned Trial Court has decided the above titled reference petition and granted the following relief:
"28.

As a result, of my aforesaid findings the reference petition is allowed and the petitioner is held entitled to enhanced compensation @ Rs. 3038/- per centiare irrespective of the classification of the acquired land.
Petitioner is also not liable for any deduction.

Besides, the petitioner is also entitled to the following relief:
i) He shall be entitled to solatium @ 30% on the market value of the land assessed herein above.
ii) He shall also be entitled for additional acquisition charges @ 12% per annum under Section 23(1A) of the Act w.e.f. 10.7.2006, i.e. from the date of notification till Land Acquisition Collector vs Rt on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90331822/
1 the date of award made by the Collector i.e. on 11.02.2008 and iii) Further, he shall be entitled to interest under Section 28 of the Act on the market value .

assessed under Section 23(1) of the Act, solatium, the additional acquisition charges worked out under Section 23(1A) of the Act @ 9% per annum from 12.2.2008 to 11.2.2009, i.e. for the period of one year and @ 15% per annum from 12.2.2009 till the amount of of payment/deposit of the amount of compensation as assessed above in the Court."
2 Parties to the lis, are hereinafter referred to, in rt the manner, in which, they were referred to, by the learned trial Court.
3. Brief facts leading to filing of the present appeal, before this Court, may be summed up as under:
The State of Himachal Pradesh issued a notification, under Section 4 of the Act, on 6.8.2005, for Sawra Kuddu Hydro Electric Project, situated in Village Chouri, Tehsil Jubbal, District Shimla.
The said notification was given wide publicity, as mandated by the Act.

Thereafter, other codal formalities were completed and award, bearing No. 585, dated 18.7.2007 was passed, by the Land Acquisition Collector, HPSEB,
Shimla.

3.1 Dissatisfied with the amount of compensation, .
the petitioners have preferred the reference petition, before the Land Acquisition Collector, who had forwarded the same to the learned District Judge, of Shimla, for adjudication.
The said reference was assigned to the learned trial Court.
3.2 rt

In the reference petition, filed under Section 18 of the Act, it has been asserted that the land,
duly described in the reference petition (hereinafter referred to as 'the suitland') has been acquired.
However, according to the petitioners, compensation, which has been awarded to them, is on the lower side.

They have asserted the market value of the land in Mauja Hatkoti, as more than Rs.
8000/- per square meter, at the time of acquisition of the land.
The Land Acquisition Officer has wrongly deducted 20%, out of the market value of the land, by ignoring the fact that the suit land was situated in developed area, having all the facilities.
They have also highlighted the potential market value of the acquired land.

4. On the basis of above facts, a prayer have been .
made to enhance the market value of the land, at the time of issuance of notification, under Section 4 of the Act @ 8000/- per square meter.

of 5. When put to notice, the reference petition has been contested by the respondents No. 1 and 3, by rt taking preliminary objections, qua the fact that petition is not maintainable; petition is bad for Land Acquisition Collector vs Rt on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90331822/
2 non-joinder of necessary parties; and that the petition is barred by limitation.
6.
On merits, paras-1 and 2 have not been disputed.
Rest of the contents of the petition have been denied.

However, the market value, as assessed in the reference petition, has been disputed/controverted, on the ground that the Land Acquisition Collector has assessed the market value, after considering all the relevant facts.
7. Respondent No. 2 has also taken almost the similar preliminary objections.
The contents of the petition have also been denied.

. 
8. From the pleadings of the parties, learned trial Court has framed the following issues, vide order dated 8.3.2016.
of 1. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the enhancement of compensation amount, as alleged?
OPP 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for statutory interest, as prayed?
OPP rt 3.
Whether the petition is not maintainable, as alleged?
OPR 4.
Whether the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as alleged?
OPR 5.
Whether the petition is barred by limitation, as alleged?

OPR 6. Relief.
9.
Thereafter, parties to the lis were directed to adduce evidence.
After closure of evidence and hearing the learned counsel for the parties, learned trial Court has decided the reference petition by awarding the relief, as referred to above.

10. Feeling aggrieved from the said award, the respondents have preferred the present appeal,
assailing the award, on the ground that the award is based upon surmises and conjunctures, as evidence adduced by the parties has been misread and mis- interpreted.
According to the respondents, the learned trial Court has not appreciated the evidence in its right perspective.

It has been further asserted that the of learned trial Court has failed to consider the fact Land Acquisition Collector vs Rt on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90331822/

12. According to the respondents, the petitioners are also not owners of land, comprised in khata No,. 4 min/20, khasra No. 304, measuring 0-02- 26 hectares, as the same had been sold by co-owners Sh. Kalam Singh and Sh. Gyan Singh to Sh. Shish Ram.

Petitioners are also not the owner of land comprised in khata No. 4, min, khatauni No. 13, khasra No. 396 and 376 measuring 0-04-81 hectares, as the same had been exchanged by co-sharer Sh.
Joginder Singh with S/Sh.
Shiv Dayal, Vijya Sain and Shyam Sunder and khasra No. 279 had not been acquired.
.
13.
The learned trial Court, according to the respondents, has wrongly enhanced the compensation and allowed uniform rates, for lands having different of classifications.

According to the them, there was no evidence to justify the award of compensation @ Rs.
rt 3,038/- per Centiare.
They have supported the rate, as awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector.
14. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the present appeal.

15. The prayer, so made, has been opposed by Mr. Ranvir Chauhan, Advocate, learned counsel appearing for respondents No. 1, 2, 3(a) to 3(c), 4 and 5 on the ground that the learned trial Court has rightly relied upon the award, Ext. PW1/B.
16.

In this case, learned trial Court, while deciding issue No. 1, has relied upon the award dated 9.10.2015, Ext. PW1/B, passed by the learned Additional District Judge-II, Shimla, Camp at Rohru,
and award dated 9.5.2014, Ext. PW1/C, passed by the learned Additional District Judge-I, Shimla,
H.P. The .
perusal of the awards shows that the subject matter of the above two awards was the land, which was acquired for Sawra Kuddu Hydro Electric Project, situated in of village Chouri, Tehsil Jubbal,
District Shimla.
17.

19. The award, Ext. PW1/C has been assailed by Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited and another, before this Court, by filing RFA No. 368 of 2014 alongwith connected matters.

The said RFAs were decided by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide judgment dated 12.10.2018.

titled as, 'The Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited and .

When, the awards, upon which, the learned trial Court has relied upon, have been modified,

23. While deciding RFA No. 368 of 2014, titled as, 'The Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited and another versus Narayan Singh & others" alongwith connected matters, a coordinate Bench of this Court has granted the following relief:
"102.

24.

disposed of accordingly by granting the same relief to the petitioners, in the present case, by exercising the powers, under Order 41 Rule 33 of the CPC.
